symbols.name: N
symbols.def: Number of donor-score replicates.

symbols.name: T
symbols.def: Number of distinct pre-event calendar windows.

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: Last event-time horizon entering buy-and-hold wealth.

symbols.name: p
symbols.def: Number of proxy coordinates at each event time.

symbols.name: d
symbols.def: \(d=p(H+1)\), the unrestricted dimension of one stacked event path.

symbols.name: S
symbols.def: Number of treated cohorts.

symbols.name: s
symbols.def: Generic treated-cohort label.

symbols.name: h
symbols.def: Generic post-event horizon.

symbols.name: t
symbols.def: Generic pre-event calendar window.

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: Indicator for the untreated or treated event path.

symbols.name: j
symbols.def: Generic donor-score replicate.

symbols.name: n_s
symbols.def: Number of replicated units in cohort \(s\) in each untreated window and at the event.

symbols.name: i
symbols.def: Generic replicated unit in cohort \(s\).

symbols.name: alpha
symbols.def: Nominal error probability for a confidence interval.

symbols.name: lambda
symbols.def: Known Holder smoothness of each untreated proxy-coordinate regression.

symbols.name: kappa
symbols.def: \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\).

symbols.name: r
symbols.def: \(r=\lfloor\lambda\rfloor\), with the usual order reduction when \(\lambda\) is an integer.

symbols.name: q_r
symbols.def: \(q_r=\binom{d+r}{r}\), the number of tensor monomials of total degree at most \(r\).

symbols.name: L
symbols.def: Common radius of the Holder regression class.

symbols.name: Holder_class
symbols.def: \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\) is the isotropic Holder ball of smoothness \(\lambda\) and radius \(L\) on \([0,1]^d\).

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: Uniform absolute bound for wealth levels and fourth-moment envelope for centered scores.

symbols.name: c_X
symbols.def: Lower bound for the pre-event path-design density.

symbols.name: C_X
symbols.def: Upper bound for the pre-event path-design density.

symbols.name: beta_0
symbols.def: Envelope constant for temporal beta-mixing coefficients.

symbols.name: rho_0
symbols.def: Geometric decay factor for temporal beta mixing.

symbols.name: c_Sigma
symbols.def: Uniform lower eigenvalue bound for the stacked donor-path covariance.

symbols.name: C_Sigma
symbols.def: Uniform upper eigenvalue bound for the stacked donor-path covariance.

symbols.name: c_mod
symbols.def: Lower constant in the attainable covariance-standardized local modulus.

symbols.name: delta_0
symbols.def: Common interior and local-modulus radius.

symbols.name: c_G
symbols.def: Coercivity threshold for a normalized local-polynomial Gram matrix.

symbols.name: c
symbols.def: Generic minimax lower-bound constant depending only on fixed class parameters.

symbols.name: C
symbols.def: Generic finite upper-bound constant depending only on fixed class parameters.

symbols.name: pi_s
symbols.def: Positive fixed weights satisfying \(\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s=1\).

symbols.name: W_si_minus
symbols.def: Pre-event wealth level of unit \(i\) in cohort \(s\).

symbols.name: R_sih_a
symbols.def: Potential simple return of unit \(i\), cohort \(s\), and horizon \(h\) under path \(a\).

symbols.name: B_si_a
symbols.def: Potential horizon-\(H\) buy-and-hold wealth for unit \(i\) in cohort \(s\) under path \(a\).

symbols.name: B_si_obs
symbols.def: Observed horizon-\(H\) event wealth for replicated treated unit \(i\) in cohort \(s\).

symbols.name: X_st
symbols.def: Exactly observed proxy path for cohort \(s\) in pre-event window \(t\).

symbols.name: f_X
symbols.def: Common density of the exact training paths.

symbols.name: Q_sti
symbols.def: Observed untreated buy-and-hold wealth for unit \(i\), cohort \(s\), and pre-event window \(t\).

symbols.name: beta_mix
symbols.def: The beta-mixing coefficients of a cohort's joint pre-event path and replicated-response calendar sequence.

symbols.name: Z_j
symbols.def: Donor replicate whose mean is the stacked realized event path.

symbols.name: z_0
symbols.def: \(z_0=(z_{01}^{\top},\ldots,z_{0S}^{\top})^{\top}\), the conditional path at which the causal contrast is evaluated.

symbols.name: hat_z
symbols.def: \(\widehat z=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{N}Z_j\).

symbols.name: Sigma
symbols.def: \(\Sigma=\operatorname{Var}(Z_j\mid z_0)\), retaining all cross-horizon, cross-coordinate, and cross-cohort covariances.

symbols.name: m_s
symbols.def: \(m_s(x)=\mathbb E[Q_{sti}\mid X_{st}=x]\), the pre-event untreated wealth regression, common across the pre-event windows.

symbols.name: mu_1s
symbols.def: \(\mu_{1s}(z_0)=\mathbb E[B_{si}(1)\mid z_0]\).

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: Joint law of the exact training paths, replicated untreated responses, donor scores, and event potential wealth levels at indices \(N,T,(n_s)_{s=1}^{S}\).

symbols.name: n_vec
symbols.def: \(\mathbf n=(n_1,\ldots,n_S)\).

symbols.name: M
symbols.def: Class \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) constructed in \texttt{def:panel-model-class}.

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: A fixed product kernel supported on the unit ball and positive on a smaller ball.

symbols.name: b_r
symbols.def: Vector of monomials of total degree at most \(r\), including the constant monomial.

symbols.name: g_sT
symbols.def: \(g_{sT}(z_0)=\inf\{b>0:\inf_{\|u-z_{0s}\|\le N^{-1/2}}\lambda_{\min}(G_{sT}(u,b))\ge c_G\}\), with value \(1\) if the set is empty.

symbols.name: omega_P
symbols.def: \(\omega_P(\delta;z_0)=\sup_{u:\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u\|_2\le\delta}|\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{m_s(z_{0s}+u_s)-m_s(z_{0s})\}|\), with feasible perturbations restricted to \(([0,1]^d)^S\).

symbols.name: R_or
symbols.def: \(R_{\mathrm{or}}=\{\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s^2n_s^{-1}\}\vee[\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}]^2\vee T^{-2\lambda/d}\).

symbols.name: R_star
symbols.def: \(R_{\star}=R_{\mathrm{or}}\vee N^{-\kappa}\).

symbols.name: hat_m_s
symbols.def: Feasible order-\(r\) tensor local-polynomial fit with replicated responses and a moving-center coercivity safeguard.

symbols.name: hat_tau
symbols.def: Replicated-donor cross-fitted local-polynomial estimator constructed in \texttt{def:frontier-estimator}.

symbols.name: tilde_tau
symbols.def: Generic competitor based on the observed panel and donor sigma-fields.

symbols.name: C_alpha
symbols.def: Bias-aware calendar-block interval constructed in \texttt{def:honest-interval}.

symbols.name: ell
symbols.def: Generic deterministic donor-fold label.

symbols.name: I_ell
symbols.def: \(I_\ell=\{j:1\le j\le N,\ j\equiv\ell\pmod {K_N}\}\), with residues represented by \(1,\ldots,K_N\).

symbols.name: bar_Z_ell
symbols.def: \(\overline Z_\ell=|I_\ell|^{-1}\sum_{j\in I_\ell}Z_j\); the balanced-fold convention makes every \(I_\ell\) nonempty for every \(N\ge1\).

symbols.name: tilde_z_ell
symbols.def: \(\widetilde z_\ell=\Pi_{([0,1]^d)^S}(\overline Z_\ell)\), where \(\Pi\) is coordinatewise Euclidean clipping to \([0,1]\).

symbols.name: hat_Sigma
symbols.def: For \(N\ge2\), spectrally clip \((N-1)^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{N}(Z_j-\widehat z)(Z_j-\widehat z)^{\top}\) to eigenvalues in \([c_\Sigma/2,2C_\Sigma]\); for \(N=1\), spectrally clip \(I_{Sd}\) to the same interval.

symbols.name: B_grid_s
symbols.def: \(\mathcal B_s=\{2^{-m}:m=0,\ldots,\lfloor\log_2(b_{0s}^{-1})\rfloor\}\), searched in increasing numerical order; it is nonempty, contains \(1\), and every candidate is at least \(b_{0s}\).

symbols.name: hat_h_sell
symbols.def: \(\widehat h_{s\ell}\) is the first element of \(\mathcal B_s\), in increasing order, for which \(\lambda_{\min}\{G_{sT}(\widetilde z_{\ell s},b)\}\ge c_G\); if the set is empty its recorded fallback value is \(1\).

symbols.name: F_fb
symbols.def: \(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}}=\{\text{at least one fold--cohort bandwidth search has an empty coercive set}\}\).

symbols.name: hat_h_s
symbols.def: \(\widehat h_s=\max_{1\le\ell\le K_N}\widehat h_{s\ell}\).

symbols.name: a_T
symbols.def: \(a_T=\lceil3\log(T\vee2)/|\log\rho_0|\rceil\).

symbols.name: b_T
symbols.def: \(b_T=\max\{1,\lfloor T^{1/2}\rfloor\}\).

symbols.name: K_T
symbols.type: number of complete retained calendar blocks
symbols.def: \(K_T=\lfloor T/(a_T+b_T)\rfloor\).

symbols.name: k
symbols.def: Generic complete retained-block label when \(K_T\ge1\).

symbols.name: J_k
symbols.def: \(J_k=\{(k-1)(a_T+b_T)+1,\ldots,(k-1)(a_T+b_T)+b_T\}\); the following \(a_T\) indices are discarded as a deterministic gap.

symbols.name: w_st
symbols.def: \(w_{st}\) is the average across donor folds of the intercept weight delivered by the selected order-\(r\) local-polynomial Gram inverse at \(\widetilde z_{\ell s}\), with the calendar fold containing \(t\) omitted when forming its score; set \(w_{st}=0\) as a bookkeeping value whenever that cross-fit inverse or training fold is undefined, and invoke the full-range interval branch.

symbols.name: Psi_k
symbols.def: \(\Psi_k=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\sum_{t\in J_k}w_{st}\{\overline Q_{st}-\widehat m_s^{(-k)}(X_{st})\}\), where \(\overline Q_{st}=n_s^{-1}\sum_iQ_{sti}\) and \(\widehat m_s^{(-k)}\) is trained on retained blocks of parity opposite to \(k\); set \(\Psi_k=0\) whenever a required cross-fit quantity has its bookkeeping value, and invoke the full-range interval branch.

symbols.name: hat_V_cal
symbols.type: centered block-sample variance in estimator scale
symbols.def: For \(K_T\ge2\), \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{cal}}=K_T(K_T-1)^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^{K_T}(\Psi_k-\overline\Psi)^2\), where \(\overline\Psi=K_T^{-1}\sum_k\Psi_k\); otherwise it is assigned the bookkeeping value \(0\) and the interval uses its full-range convention.

symbols.name: hat_V_Bs
symbols.def: For \(n_s\ge2\), \(\widehat V_{B,s}=(n_s-1)^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\overline B_s^{\mathrm{obs}})^2\), where \(\overline B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}=n_s^{-1}\sum_iB_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\); otherwise it is assigned \(0\) and the interval uses its full-range convention.

symbols.name: hat_se
symbols.def: \(\widehat{\operatorname{se}}=\{\widehat V_{\mathrm{cal}}+\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s^2\widehat V_{B,s}/n_s\}^{1/2}\).

symbols.name: alpha_st
symbols.def: \(\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}=\alpha/2\).

symbols.name: alpha_don
symbols.def: \(\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}=\alpha/2\), so \(\alpha=\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}\).

symbols.name: z_crit
symbols.def: \(z_{\mathrm{crit}}=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}/2)\).

symbols.name: q_don
symbols.def: \(q_{\mathrm{don}}=\sqrt{Sd/\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}}\), the fixed-dimensional second-moment Markov radius implied by the maintained fourth-moment bound; the operational ellipsoid is defined with \(\widehat\Sigma\).

symbols.name: C_H
symbols.def: A deterministic constant depending only on \(L,d,r,K,c_\Sigma,C_\Sigma,c_G\) and dominating the local-polynomial and covariance-comparison Holder remainders.

symbols.name: R_alpha
symbols.def: \(R_\alpha=z_{\mathrm{crit}}\widehat{\operatorname{se}}+C_H\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\widehat h_s^\lambda+C_H(q_{\mathrm{don}}/\sqrt N)^\kappa\).

symbols.name: P_ex
symbols.def: The bounded, noisy law constructed in \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp} to demonstrate non-vacuity of the attainable-direction condition.

standard.name: consistency for the realized treatment path

novel.justification: This cross-date counterfactual equality is untestable from the observed design. Short-window institutional stability after conditioning on a rich fixed-dimensional market path can motivate it, but that story is not evidence for the equality. Rolling untreated pseudo-events can diagnose or falsify pre-event stability and cannot verify transport to the untreated event-date counterfactual.

assumptions.condition: For every cohort, \(m_s\) belongs to the isotropic Holder ball \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\) on \([0,1]^d\).
The exact training paths have density satisfying \(c_X\le f_X(x)\le C_X\) for every \(x\in[0,1]^d\).

standard.name: regular random design with density bounded away from zero

assumptions.condition: Conditional on the path-design array and \(z_0\), the unit histories are mutually independent across \((s,i)\).

standard.name: conditional cross-unit independence in many-control panels

assumptions.condition: Conditional on \(z_0\), the donor scores \((Z_j)_{j=1}^{N}\) are independent and identically distributed.
For every cohort, the joint pre-event calendar sequence \(((X_{st},(Q_{sti})_{i=1}^{n_s}))_{t=1}^{T}\) has beta-mixing coefficients satisfying \(\beta(k)\le\beta_0\rho_0^k\) for every \(k\ge1\).

standard.name: geometric beta mixing for calendar sequences

assumptions.condition: Every \(X_{st}\) is observed without donor measurement error in the response-regression sigma-field.

novel.justification: This data architecture occurs when historical market-state paths are recorded directly while only the event-date counterfactual path is synthesized from donors. It is empirically distinguishable from applying an estimated proxy map to every training row and from observing classically contaminated training coordinates.

assumptions.condition: Conditional on \(z_0\), the donor-score sample is independent of the exact training array and the treated event outcomes.

standard.name: sample splitting for evaluation at an estimated center

assumptions.condition: The full covariance satisfies \(c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd}\).

standard.name: bounded fourth moment for covariance estimation

novel.justification: This is a disclosed, maintained one-direction condition on the pre-event regression functional and is not derived from Holder smoothness. It is realistic for a non-affine surface with nonzero covariance-standardized gradient when \(\kappa=1\) and for an asymmetric standardized cusp when \(0<\kappa<1\), as demonstrated by \texttt{prop:worked-modulus-example}.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}=\{P_{N,T,(n_s)_{s=1}^{S}}:P_{N,T,(n_s)_{s=1}^{S}}\text{ satisfies all listed causal, smoothness, support, dependence, observation-structure, moment, covariance, and modulus conditions}\}\).

definitions.name: Uniform moving-center Gram radius
definitions.construction: For each \(s\), form \(G_{sT}(u,b)\) from the exactly observed \(X_{st}\) and set \(g_{sT}(z_0)=\inf\{b>0:\inf_{\|u-z_{0s}\|_2\le N^{-1/2}}\lambda_{\min}(G_{sT}(u,b))\ge c_G\}\), with fallback value \(1\).

definitions.name: Four-channel phase diagram
definitions.construction: \(R_{\mathrm{or}}=\{\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s^2/n_s\}\vee[\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}]^2\vee T^{-2\lambda/d}\) and \(R_{\star}=R_{\mathrm{or}}\vee N^{-\kappa}\), whose four entries are treated-mean noise, replicated-response smoothing, random-design spacing, and generated-path uncertainty.

definitions.name: Replicated-donor cross-fitted local-polynomial estimator
definitions.construction: Set \(K_N=\min\{2,N\}\), assign donors to the deterministic balanced folds \(I_\ell\), compute \(\overline Z_\ell\), and replace every raw fold mean by \(\widetilde z_\ell=\Pi_{([0,1]^d)^S}(\overline Z_\ell)\). The coordinatewise projection is Borel measurable and Euclidean nonexpansive relative to the interior center \(z_0\); covariance ellipticity therefore gives \(\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\widetilde z_\ell-z_0)\|_2\le(C_\Sigma/c_\Sigma)^{1/2}\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\overline Z_\ell-z_0)\|_2\). Form \(\overline Q_{st}=n_s^{-1}\sum_iQ_{sti}\). For each \((s,\ell)\), search \(\mathcal B_s\) in deterministic increasing order and take the first \(b\) with \(\lambda_{\min}\{G_{sT}(\widetilde z_{\ell s},b)\}\ge c_G\); all eigenvalue ties are accepted at equality. At that bandwidth use the unique order-\(r\) tensor local-polynomial intercept and clip its fitted value to \([-B,B]\). If the coercive set is empty, record \(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}}\) and define that fold--cohort value as \(\operatorname{clip}_{[-B,B]}\{(Tn_s)^{-1}\sum_{t,i}Q_{sti}\}\), with recorded bandwidth \(1\). Average the clipped values over \(\ell=1,\ldots,K_N\) to define \(\widehat m_s\), and set \(\widehat\tau=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{n_s^{-1}\sum_iB_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat m_s\}\). Thus \(\widehat\tau\in[-2B,2B]\) is measurable and defined for every \(N,T,n_s\ge1\), including every empty coercive search.

definitions.name: Calendar-block full-covariance interval
definitions.construction: Fix \(\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}=\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}=\alpha/2\). Use complete retained blocks \(J_k=\{(k-1)(a_T+b_T)+1,\ldots,(k-1)(a_T+b_T)+b_T\}\) for \(k=1,\ldots,K_T\), with \(a_T=\lceil3\log(T\vee2)/|\log\rho_0|\rceil\), \(b_T=\max\{1,\lfloor T^{1/2}\rfloor\}\), and the following \(a_T\) observations discarded after each retained block. Split retained blocks by odd and even \(k\); for each block form \(\Psi_k\) using a fit trained on the opposite parity and the actual selected local-polynomial weights \(w_{st}\). For \(K_T\ge2\), set \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{cal}}=K_T(K_T-1)^{-1}\sum_k(\Psi_k-\overline\Psi)^2\), and add \(\sum_s\pi_s^2\widehat V_{B,s}/n_s\) to obtain \(\widehat{\operatorname{se}}^2\). For \(N\ge2\), use the full donor sample covariance and spectrally clip its eigenvalues to \([c_\Sigma/2,2C_\Sigma]\); for \(N=1\), clip \(I_{Sd}\) and invoke the full-range convention below. With \(q_{\mathrm{don}}=\sqrt{Sd/\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}}\), use the \(\widehat\Sigma\)-ellipsoid of radius \(q_{\mathrm{don}}/\sqrt N\), set \(R_\alpha=z_{\mathrm{crit}}\widehat{\operatorname{se}}+C_H\sum_s\pi_s\widehat h_s^\lambda+C_H(q_{\mathrm{don}}/\sqrt N)^\kappa\), and define \(C_\alpha=[\widehat\tau-R_\alpha,\widehat\tau+R_\alpha]\cap[-2B,2B]\). All block, parity, grid, and equality tie-breaking rules are deterministic. If fewer than two retained blocks have finite non-bookkeeping scores, \(N<2\), some \(n_s<2\), an opposite-parity training fold is empty, any denominator is undefined, any numerical input is nonfinite, or \(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}}\) occurs, define \(C_\alpha=[-2B,2B]\).

definitions.name: Bounded non-affine attainable-direction DGP
definitions.construction: Fix admissible class constants with \(c_\Sigma\le1/2\), \(C_\Sigma\ge1\), and \(B^4\ge(Sd)^2\). Set \(z_0=\tfrac12\mathbf 1_{Sd}\), draw the \(X_{st}\) independently and uniformly on \([0,1]^d\), and take \(\Sigma=\tfrac12I_{Sd}+\tfrac{1}{2Sd}\mathbf 1_{Sd}\mathbf 1_{Sd}^{\top}\). For independent Rademacher vectors \(U_j\in\{-1,1\}^{Sd}\), set \(Z_j=z_0+\Sigma^{1/2}U_j\). Put \(a_0=\min\{B,L,1\}/64\), \(\bar e=(e_1^{\top},0,\ldots,0)^{\top}\), and \(q_0=(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{1/2}\). Choose \(\delta_0\le\min\{1/2,\{2\|\Sigma\bar e/q_0\|_\infty\}^{-1}\}\) and \(c_{\mathrm{mod}}\le\pi_1a_0\min\{q_0,q_0^{\kappa}\}\). If \(\kappa=1\), set \(m_1(x)=4a_0+a_0(x_1-1/2)+a_0(x_1-1/2)^2\); if \(0<\kappa<1\), set \(m_1(x)=4a_0+a_0(x_1-1/2)_+^{\kappa}-(a_0/2)(1/2-x_1)_+^{\kappa}\); and set \(m_s(x)=4a_0\) for \(s>1\). With mutually independent centered Rademacher noises \(\varepsilon_{sti}\) and \(\eta_{si}\), define \(Q_{sti}=m_s(X_{st})+a_0\varepsilon_{sti}\), \(B_{si}(0)=m_s(z_{0s})+a_0\eta_{si}\), \(B_{si}(1)=B_{si}(0)+a_0\), and \(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{si}(1)\). Finally take \(W_{si,-1}=1\), \(R_{si0}(a)=B_{si}(a)-1\), and \(R_{sih}(a)=0\) for \(h>0\). These prescriptions define \(P_{\mathrm{ex}}\).

definitions.name: Product-experiment ordered-modulus handle
definitions.construction: Solve the conditional ordered-modulus problem for the product of the treated-mean, replicated-regression, realized-design-hole, and full-covariance donor-location experiments, then invert the resulting least-favorable tests using the calendar-block score as the stochastic coordinate.

statements.statement: For every law \(P\), consistency and event-date counterfactual transport alone imply \(\tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\}\).
statements.justification: This isolates causal identification from the estimation frontier and keeps the target a level-wealth contrast rather than a return approximation.
statements.gap: Ferman (2021) obtains factor-loading recovery for synthetic controls; it does not identify this nonlinear realized-path wealth regression functional.
statements.consumer: Financial event studies can report an interpretable dollar-wealth effect while using rolling untreated pseudo-events only to diagnose or falsify pre-event stability, not to verify event-date transport.

statements.statement: Conditional on \(z_0\) and the exact path-design array, the likelihood under \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) factors into a direct replicated-regression experiment, a treated-mean experiment, and an independent finite-dimensional donor-location experiment with covariance \(\Sigma\). No convolution operator acts on the training coordinates \(X_{st}\).
statements.justification: The factorization is the early-kill boundary separating a generated query location from an errors-in-variables training design.
statements.gap: Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012) generate every training coordinate, while Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008) observe classically contaminated training coordinates; neither experiment has this factorization.
statements.consumer: Applied analysts can determine from data provenance whether donor uncertainty requires a Holder modulus correction or a deconvolution analysis.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) and \(0<\delta\le\delta_0\), \[c_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta^{\kappa}\le\omega_P(\delta;z_0)\le C\delta^{\kappa}.\] The upper inequality follows from Holder smoothness and covariance ellipticity. The lower inequality is exactly the disclosed one-direction condition \texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus} and is not derived from the other panel conditions.
statements.justification: The lemma pairs the derived Holder upper bound with the explicitly maintained one-direction lower condition needed for matching donor-location converses.
statements.gap: Donoho (1994) fixes a Gaussian operator and convex class; this modulus uses an unknown full stacked donor covariance and avoids a multidirectional co-Holder condition that a scalar regression cannot satisfy.
statements.consumer: The event-study estimator can calibrate one covariance-aware proxy-bias radius while the lower bound remains legal on nondegenerate multivariate path neighborhoods.

statements.statement: The law \(P_{\mathrm{ex}}\) in \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp} belongs to \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) for the displayed admissible constants and is nondegenerate: its responses have bounded nonzero conditional noise, its design point is interior, and its full stacked donor covariance is positive definite with nonzero off-diagonal entries. Let \(\bar e=(e_1^{\top},0,\ldots,0)^{\top}\in\mathbb R^{Sd}\) and \(u_\delta=\delta\Sigma\bar e/(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{1/2}\). Then \(\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_\delta\|_2=\delta\) and \(\bar e^{\top}u_\delta=\delta(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{1/2}>0\). Consequently, when \(\kappa=1\), the weighted surface has nonzero standardized gradient and its increment along \(u_\delta\) is \(\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{1/2}\delta/64+O(\delta^2)\); when \(0<\kappa<1\), the positive asymmetric-cusp increment is \(\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{\kappa/2}\delta^{\kappa}/64\). Hence \(\omega_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}(\delta;z_0)\asymp\delta^{\kappa}\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\). This construction establishes non-vacuity only and does not derive the lower modulus for the general panel class.
statements.justification: The explicit calculation shows that the maintained lower-modulus condition is compatible with bounded noisy panel laws and non-affine response surfaces.
statements.gap: The general frontier assumes one attainable Mahalanobis direction; this proposition supplies a concrete nondegenerate member rather than claiming that Holder smoothness alone implies attainability.
statements.consumer: Referees can audit the donor lower-bound channel on a legal bounded DGP before assessing the general conditional minimax proof.

statements.statement: For every \(N,T,n_s\ge1\), each map \(\overline Z_\ell\mapsto\widetilde z_\ell\) is Borel measurable and satisfies \(\|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2\le\|\overline Z_\ell-z_0\|_2\) and \(\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\widetilde z_\ell-z_0)\|_2\le(C_\Sigma/c_\Sigma)^{1/2}\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\overline Z_\ell-z_0)\|_2\). The finite dyadic grid is nonempty and its deterministic first-coercive rule, clipped pooled-mean fallback, clipped fitted values, covariance spectral clipping, and small-sample conventions make \(\widehat\tau\) and \(C_\alpha\) measurable and samplewise defined. Moreover, \(\widehat\tau\in[-2B,2B]\), and \(C_\alpha\) equals the displayed radius interval on the regular branch and \([-2B,2B]\) on every declared bad branch.
statements.justification: The inferential claims require procedures defined on bad donor, design, and small-sample realizations rather than only on the asymptotically regular event.
statements.gap: Akhavan, Gogolashvili, and Tsybakov (2024) regularize point evaluation at an estimated minimizer, while Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) totalize a different synthetic-control prediction procedure; neither supplies these generated-center and moving-Gram conventions.
statements.consumer: The frontier and coverage proofs can integrate over exceptional samples without silently assigning an estimator or variance to an empty inverse or undefined denominator.

statements.statement: Conditional on the disclosed one-direction condition \texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus}, there exist constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on the fixed class parameters, such that for every growth array with \(N\wedge T\wedge\min_s n_s\to\infty\), every interior realized path \(z_0\), and every exact design array with \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\), \[cR_D\le\inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}\mathbb E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau(z_0))^2\mid z_0,(X_{st})]\le\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau(z_0))^2\mid z_0,(X_{st})]\le CR_D.\] The lower bound is witnessed inside the same causal class by separate treated-mean, replicated Holder-bump, empty-neighborhood, and covariance-aligned donor-location subexperiments; specifically, the \(N^{-\kappa}\) converse uses the maintained direction. The upper-bound assertion includes a uniform bound on \(\Pr_P(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}}\mid z_0,(X_{st}))\) strong enough that the squared error of the clipped pooled-mean fallback is absorbed by \(R_D\); the proof must count that event and may not analyze it as regular Gram geometry. The total feasible estimator has no additional tensor-Gram or deconvolution phase.
statements.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: it resolves the four information channels on every relative-growth regime before averaging over random design geometry.
statements.gap: Fan (1993) and Fan et al. (1997) treat ordinary pointwise smoothing; Akhavan, Gogolashvili, and Tsybakov (2024) evaluate at an estimated minimizer. None gives a causal replicated-site frontier with an external nonregular donor center, realized holes, arbitrary sample-size ratios, and four same-class converses.
statements.consumer: Researchers can read the active bottleneck directly from observed cohort replication, calendar coverage, and donor count, and can avoid unnecessary Fourier deconvolution when only the event query is generated.

statements.statement: Under the regular random-design law and conditional on \texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus}, averaging the conditional frontier over \((X_{st})\) gives \[\inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}\mathbb E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau(z_0))^2\mid z_0]\asymp R_{\star}.\] The \(N^{-\kappa}\) converse, and therefore the four-channel equivalence, is conditional on that maintained direction. Thus the oracle region is \(N^{-\kappa}=o(R_{\mathrm{or}})\), the generated-proxy region is \(R_{\mathrm{or}}=o(N^{-\kappa})\), and their boundary is \(N\asymp R_{\mathrm{or}}^{-1/\kappa}\), where \(R_{\mathrm{or}}\) is the maximum of the treated-mean, replicated-smoothing, and spacing terms. For \(S=1\), \(H=0\), \(p=d=1\), and \(n_1=n\), the rate reduces to \(n^{-1}\vee(Tn)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+1)}\vee T^{-2\lambda}\vee N^{-\lambda}\) when \(0<\lambda\le1\).
statements.justification: The result turns the realized-geometry theorem into an explicit phase diagram and discharges the scalar early-kill test without a pointwise logarithm.
statements.gap: Stone (1982) gives the ordinary \(d\)-dimensional smoothing exponent and Gaiffas (2007) gives a spatially normalized global sup-risk with a logarithm; neither separates replication saturation, pointwise spacing, and an external donor modulus.
statements.consumer: Power calculations for event studies can trade additional donors, longer pre-event histories, and more within-cohort replication on a common risk scale.

statements.statement: Conditional on \texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus}, the interval \(C_\alpha=[\widehat\tau-R_\alpha,\widehat\tau+R_\alpha]\cap[-2B,2B]\) on the regular branch, and \(C_\alpha=[-2B,2B]\) under every declared bad-sample convention, satisfies \[\liminf\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}\Pr_P\{\tau(z_0)\in C_\alpha\mid z_0\}\ge1-\alpha,\qquad\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid z_0]\le C R_{\star}^{1/2}.\] The proof must uniformly bound the probability of fewer than two usable blocks, undefined variance denominators, donor-covariance small samples, empty opposite-parity fits, and \(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}}\), and must include the full-range interval's length on those events. Conversely, every interval with the same uniform conditional coverage has worst-case conditional expected length at least \(cR_{\star}^{1/2}\). The \(N^{-\kappa/2}\) expected-length converse, and hence the four-channel length equivalence, uses the maintained direction. The separated calendar-block construction uses actual local-polynomial weights and the full spectrally clipped \(\widehat\Sigma\), and incurs no multiplicative logarithmic phase.
statements.justification: Point estimation alone does not resolve whether proxy and spacing bias can be covered honestly without sacrificing a logarithmic factor.
statements.gap: Armstrong and Kolesar (2020) calibrate bias-aware intervals after assuming a uniform centered limit, while Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) handle dependent synthetic-control prediction. Neither derives a phase-uniform shrinking confidence interval for this nonregular causal mean.
statements.consumer: The interval gives event-study users conditional coverage and a sample-size diagnostic even when smoothing bias or donor-path uncertainty is first order.

statements.statement: Can the order-optimal interval be replaced by a total feasible interval whose conditional expected length attains the exact asymptotic minimax constant simultaneously at every intersection of the four phases, while estimating the full donor covariance and the calendar long-run variance? The handle is the product-experiment ordered-modulus construction in \texttt{def:sharp-constant-handle}, with least-favorable tests calibrated after the moving-center Gram perturbation is controlled.
statements.justification: Rate optimality does not identify the joint least-favorable law when two or more nonregular channels bind at once.
statements.gap: Donoho (1994) and Armstrong and Kolesar (2018) solve Gaussian convex-class modulus problems with fixed operators; the product experiment here has random geometry, a Holder donor location, and estimated dependence.
statements.consumer: An exact constant would support principled allocation of sampling resources when donor, calendar, and replication costs place an application near a phase boundary.

sampling_model.design: For each fixed cohort, \(T\) exact pre-event proxy paths are drawn from a density bounded above and away from zero on \([0,1]^d\); the theorem first conditions on their realized local-polynomial geometry.
sampling_model.units: Each cohort supplies \(n_s\) replicated untreated wealth blocks per pre-event window and \(n_s\) treated event wealth levels; histories are conditionally independent across units and geometrically beta-mixing across calendar windows.
sampling_model.treatment: A cohort enters the event path once. Consistency links observed event wealth to treated potential wealth, and the explicitly maintained event-date transport equality supplies the untreated conditional mean. The observed design cannot test that cross-date counterfactual equality.
sampling_model.overlap: Every realized cohort path is at least \(\delta_0\) from the boundary of \([0,1]^d\), and the training density is at least \(c_X\) there.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The event path is the mean of \(N\) donor scores with unknown full covariance \(\Sigma\). Every foldwise donor mean is projected coordinatewise onto \(([0,1]^d)^S\), covariance eigenvalues are clipped to \([c_\Sigma/2,2C_\Sigma]\), and a deterministic finite dyadic bandwidth search has a clipped pooled-response fallback. Separated calendar blocks use fixed gap and block sequences; training coordinates are exactly observed, so donor noise moves only the evaluation center.

estimand_functional: \(\tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\},\quad \operatorname{MSE}(\widehat\tau)\asymp R_{\star}\text{ conditional on event-date transport and the attainable-direction restriction}\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 7 gives the fixed-point local-polynomial squared-risk rate, and Theorem 8 evaluates that estimator at an independent estimated minimizer under strong convexity.
Theorem 1 expands a local-linear regression estimator when an estimated covariate is attached to every training observation.
Theorems 3.1--3.6 recover known-error deconvolution performance when every latent training coordinate is observed with replicated classical error.
The optimal finite-\(q\) norm rate for a derivative of order \(m\) of a \(p\)-smooth \(d\)-dimensional regression is \(n^{-(p-m)/(2p+d)}\).
Local-linear smoothers attain the ordinary pointwise minimax order and high asymptotic minimax efficiency under fixed or random design.
Ordered moduli yield finite-sample optimal confidence intervals for linear functionals over convex regression classes in a known Gaussian experiment.
Bias-aware local-polynomial intervals have uniform asymptotic coverage and near-optimal length when a centered uniform limit and worst-case bias bound are available.
Synthetic-control prediction intervals account for weight-estimation and post-treatment innovation uncertainty, with a beta-mixing extension based on block coupling.
Proposition 3.1 gives synthetic-control factor-loading recovery and weight dilution when controls and pre-treatment periods jointly grow.

tldr: The causal target is cohort-weighted buy-and-hold level wealth at a fixed realized event path, identified by consistency and an explicitly untestable event-date counterfactual transport equality. Historical proxy paths are observed exactly, whereas the event path alone is generated from an independent donor sample with unknown full covariance. This sigma-field distinction converts donor uncertainty into a covariance-standardized Holder location modulus rather than a deconvolution operator. Conditional on a disclosed one-direction lower-modulus condition, the kernel is a conditional minimax theorem over realized local-polynomial geometry, an explicit four-channel marginal phase diagram across arbitrary donor, calendar, and replication growth, and a matching uniformly honest expected-length frontier. Projected donor centers, a deterministic finite bandwidth grid, clipped fits, and a full-range bad-sample interval make both procedures samplewise total. A bounded non-affine worked DGP establishes non-vacuity of the maintained direction; exact constants at phase intersections remain open.

project_justification.gap: Classical nonparametric regression fixes the evaluation point, generated-regressor expansions perturb every training coordinate, and measurement-error regression convolves every latent training coordinate. Synthetic-control inference likewise does not separate replicated smoothing, random spacing, and an external nonregular donor center in one causal experiment.
project_justification.niche: Event studies often record historical market paths directly but synthesize only the event-date untreated path from donors. With many units per calendar window, response noise can vanish faster than the spatial resolution of the finite set of historical paths, exposing a spacing phase that ordinary one-observation-per-site asymptotics suppress.
project_justification.fill: The project separates the pre-event regression from the untestable event-date transport premise, states the observation sigma-fields, conditions first on realized Gram geometry, and derives the maximum of treated noise, replicated smoothing, spacing, and covariance-standardized donor uncertainty conditional on a disclosed attainable direction. It constructs a samplewise total cross-fitted estimator using projected fold centers, a finite first-coercive bandwidth rule, clipped fits, and a pooled-mean fallback. Its explicit block interval uses centered influence-score block variance, treated-mean variance, a fourth-moment donor radius, spectral covariance clipping, and a conservative full-range value on every bad sample. Matching estimation and expected-length lower bounds remain in the same causal class, and a bounded non-affine DGP demonstrates that the direction condition is non-vacuous.

related_work: Stone (1982), Fan (1993), and Fan et al. (1997) provide the ordinary Holder and local-polynomial benchmark, including multivariate Gram and minimax calculations, but have neither site replication nor a generated query. Gaiffas (2007) establishes spatially normalized global sup-risk under inhomogeneous random design; its logarithm belongs to uniform spatial loss and does not settle the realized-point spacing term here. Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012) derive a differentiable stochastic expansion when generated coordinates enter every training row. Hahn and Ridder (2013) derive pathwise influence corrections for smooth generated regressors. Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008) and Fan and Truong (1993) study the different experiment in which every training coordinate is classically contaminated and Fourier inversion is required. Akhavan, Gogolashvili, and Tsybakov (2024) is the closest clean-training random-center construction: its Theorems 7 and 8 sample-split an estimated minimizer from a regularized local-polynomial evaluation, but strong convexity makes center error second order and removes a separate external \(N^{-\kappa}\) phase. Donoho (1994), Low (1997), and Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, 2020) supply modulus and bias-aware honest-inference machinery for fixed Gaussian or ordinary regression experiments. Ferman (2021) organizes simultaneous donor and period growth through factor recovery. Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) supply a full-covariance dependent synthetic-control prediction template, while Chernozhukov, Wuthrich, and Zhu (2021) already occupy the conformal block-permutation route. Abadie (2021) and Arkhangelsky and Imbens (2024) locate the result within synthetic-control and causal-panel practice.
technical_internal_limitation: The no-deconvolution conclusion is conditional on the exact observation structure. If an estimated proxy map is applied to every pre-event row, the Mammen--Rothe--Schienle generated-regressor expansion becomes relevant; if only noisy replicates of every latent training coordinate are observed, the Delaigle--Hall--Meister deconvolution experiment applies. Cross-fitting alone does not convert either design into a generated-center experiment. The pointwise spacing term is \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\); uniform coverage over every path in the cube would generally replace it by a logarithmically inflated global fill-distance term. Totalization does not permit exceptional samples to be ignored: the upper-bound and expected-length proofs must bound the probability of every bandwidth fallback, inadequate block count, and undefined raw variance denominator, including the full-range interval's contribution. The worked law \(P_{\mathrm{ex}}\) establishes only that the attainable-direction restriction is non-vacuous; it does not derive that restriction for the general panel class.
honest_scope: The event-date transport equality is a maintained cross-date counterfactual restriction that the observed design cannot test. Rolling untreated pseudo-events can diagnose or falsify stability within the pre-event period, but cannot verify transport to the untreated event date; an institutional stability story is motivation rather than evidence. The \(N^{-\kappa}\) MSE converse and the \(N^{-\kappa/2}\) expected-length converse are conditional on \texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus}, so Theorems 1--3 and the proposal are capped at field tier. The effective dimension is \(d=p(H+1)\) because the stacked path is unrestricted; a \(d=p\) claim would require an additional shared-index structure and is not made. The scalar \(H=0\), \(S=p=d=1\), and \(0<\lambda\le1\) reduction is explicit in Theorem 2. Exact minimax constants, automatic smoothness adaptation, growing path dimension, and uniform-in-path bands remain open.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace a generated coordinate on every training row by an independent generated evaluation center, then prove uniform Gram coercivity on its Mahalanobis neighborhood before applying the Holder modulus.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for replicated-site regression at an external generated center found Akhavan--Gogolashvili--Tsybakov (2024), but no conditional four-channel causal minimax and honest-length theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Akhavan--Gogolashvili--Tsybakov Theorem 8, Stone, and a triangle inequality.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their center is a minimizer of the same smooth strongly convex regression, so its effect is second order and dominated; they do not have external donor scaling, Holder cusps, replication saturation, realized holes, calendar dependence, or honest-length converses.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Express the three data architectures as distinct likelihood factorizations and determine exactly when a convolution operator enters the training experiment.
seed_details.destination_search: Generated-regressor, errors-in-variables, and random-center searches found each architecture separately but no necessary-and-sufficient experiment-comparison theorem joining them.
seed_details.red_team: This is only a taxonomy pasting three known literatures.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds unless upgraded to a deficiency or iff theorem, so the factorization is retained only as a supporting lemma rather than the headline.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Derive a stable joint limit for calendar-block local-polynomial scores, realized Gram geometry, and the covariance-standardized generated center before applying any pivotal calibration.
seed_details.destination_search: Mixing local-polynomial limit theory and synthetic-control prediction intervals do not characterize necessity of Gaussian centering at proxy and spacing phase boundaries.
seed_details.red_team: The cusp term is only a generalized delta method added to an existing mixing central limit theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: A universal cusp limit is unavailable over the full Holder ball; the credible object is a least-favorable limit experiment or pivotality frontier, so this seed is deferred behind the rate theorem.

seed_details.destination_search: Hahn--Ridder covers differentiable generated regressors, and point evaluation is not pathwise differentiable over the full finite-Holder class.
seed_details.red_team: The regular-phase efficiency bound is an immediate delta-method variance formula.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for the stated broad class; a separate efficiency paper would require a narrower regular tangent model and materially new shared-cell covariance structure.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Build a symmetry orbit jointly for donor centers and overlapping calendar blocks, then invert pathwise counterfactual nulls.
seed_details.destination_search: Conformal synthetic-control inference and dependent block permutations are already occupied, while conditional-on-realized-path mean coverage lacks the required exact symmetry.
seed_details.red_team: The method is already Chernozhukov--Wuthrich--Zhu with a different conformity score.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds, and imposing stronger symmetry would change the intended model merely to fit the motif.

seed_details.destination_search: Synthetic-control donor weighting is an inferential nuisance choice, not a causal treatment policy with a defined welfare value in this topic.
seed_details.red_team: Donor allocation is experimental design or nuisance tuning, not policy learning.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds because no intervention policy or welfare regret is induced by choosing donor scores.

literature_map.settled: Ordinary \(d\)-dimensional Holder smoothing rates, local-polynomial Gram methods, and global inhomogeneous-design sup-risk are established.
literature_map.open_boundary: A realized-point experiment with only \(T\) distinct sites, \(n_s\) response replicates per site, and a separate spatial-resolution floor is not covered.

literature_map.settled: Smooth stochastic expansions are available when generated regressors enter training rows, and sample splitting can evaluate a clean regression at an estimated strongly convex minimizer.
literature_map.open_boundary: No result treats an external root-\(N\) center with a \(\kappa\)-Holder covariance-standardized modulus as a distinct minimax and honest-length phase.

literature_map.settled: Classical noisy training coordinates induce a convolution inverse problem; replication can recover known-error deconvolution performance.
literature_map.open_boundary: These rates do not apply when training coordinates are exact and only the query center is donor-generated.

literature_map.settled: Gaussian convex-class moduli characterize near-minimax estimation and confidence length, and bias-aware local-polynomial intervals are available after a uniform centered limit is established.
literature_map.open_boundary: The operator here is a product of random geometry, dependent regression, treated means, and a nonregular donor location with estimated covariance.

literature_map.settled: Many-control factor recovery, dependent prediction intervals, conformal block inversion, and practical panel design guidance are available.
literature_map.open_boundary: They do not deliver a conditional shrinking confidence interval for realized-path level wealth at the four-channel minimax rate.

novelty_justification.precise_gap: Akhavan--Gogolashvili--Tsybakov evaluate a clean regression at an estimated minimizer, but strong convexity makes center error second order and their one-sample passive-design problem has no external donor phase, replicated-site spacing, causal target, or honest interval. Cattaneo--Feng--Titiunik provide full-covariance conditional prediction under dependence, but not Holder smoothing or a shrinking causal-mean expected-length frontier.
novelty_justification.strict_delta: Relative to the ordinary fixed-point rate, the theorem derives the additional \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\) barrier from finite path-space resolution and, conditional on the disclosed attainable direction, the \(N^{-\kappa}\) barrier from the external donor modulus. It proves that the active barriers enter as a maximum rather than through a deconvolution exponent or a fifth moving-Gram phase.
novelty_justification.search_conclusion: Target--method searches across generated regressors, random-center regression, replicated measurement error, pointwise random design, synthetic-control prediction, and honest nonparametric intervals found no closer paper that subsumes the combined conditional frontier and matching expected-length claim.

message: Revised the preserved field-tier four-channel frontier with samplewise-total projected-center estimation, deterministic bandwidth fallback, and an explicit conservative calendar-block interval. The proposal gate passed with zero violations, and the rendered LaTeX compiled successfully.
